newsitem.title: GERMANY: IMF head urges Europe to help poorer countries.
newsitem.headline: IMF head urges Europe to help poorer countries.

text.p: International Monetary Fund (IMF) president Michel Camdessus on Friday urged European countries not to ignore the interests of their poorer neighbours.
Europe should take a more active role in improving conditions for the world's poorest countries, Camdessus said at a meeting of Germany's Christian Social Union political party.

German Finance Minister Theo Waigel, head of the CSU, has been one of the most outspoken opponents of an IMF plan to sell gold to support the world's poorest countries. A decision on the issue, postponed last September, is still pending.
Camdessus said a quick decision is needed this spring on fresh financing for the IMF, so that it could do more for the world's less developed nations.
The IMF chief also called on Germany and other European countries to adopt structural economic reforms to improve their competitiveness.
If that doesn't happen, they will fall behind trading partners that are embracing globalisation, he said.
He said the competitive potential of Germany and Europe is greater than many people believe.
